subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Obtain the reduction formula for I_n = ∫ cotⁿx dx, n being a positive integer, n ≥ 2, and deduce the value of ∫ cot⁴x dx.

mark_split.label: Set up the split cotⁿx = cotⁿ⁻²x(csc²x − 1)
Integrate by substitution and box the reduction formula

insider_note: cotⁿx mirrors tanⁿx term for term with cot and csc swapped in for tan and sec — learn tanⁿ's reduction and this one is the same working with every letter relabelled.

steps.label: Set up the split cotⁿx = cotⁿ⁻²x(csc²x − 1)
lines: Let I_n = ∫ cotⁿx dx = ∫ cotⁿ⁻²x · cot²x dx
steps.why: cot²x = csc²x − 1 is the cotangent partner of tan²x = sec²x − 1, and splits the integral the same way — one substitutable piece, one lower power of cotx.
common_mistakes: Using tan²x = sec²x − 1 by mistake instead of the cotangent identity.
Writing csc²x − 1 as 1 − csc²x, flipping the sign.
steps.memory_tip: cot²x + 1 = csc²x, so cot²x = csc²x − 1 — the cotangent twin of tan²x = sec²x − 1.

steps.label: Integrate by substitution and box the reduction formula
lines: In the first integral put t = cotx ⇒ dt = −csc²x dx
steps.why: cotx differentiates to −csc²x, one sign different from tanx, so the substitution here picks up an extra minus sign that the tanⁿx reduction does not have.
common_mistakes: Missing the minus sign that comes from dt = −csc²x dx, which copies the tanⁿx formula unchanged.
Writing the second term as +I_{n−2} instead of −I_{n−2}.
steps.memory_tip: cotx's derivative carries a minus that tanx's does not — that minus is the only difference from the tanⁿ formula.

steps.label: Substitute n = 4, 2 down to I₀
steps.why: n = 4 needs I₂, and I₂ needs I₀ = x — the same even-n chain used for every other power reduction in this chapter, just carrying cotx's extra minus sign at each step.
common_mistakes: Chaining down to I₁ instead of I₀, which is the odd-n stopping point.
Losing a minus sign at each substitution, since every term in this reduction is negative.
steps.memory_tip: Every term in this reduction is negative — if a plus sign appears anywhere, re-check it.

steps.label: Combine for the final answer
steps.why: Subtracting the negative I₂ flips both its terms positive, which is why the final answer for cot⁴x ends up with a plus sign on cotx and on x despite every earlier line being negative.
common_mistakes: Not distributing the minus sign across both terms of (−cotx − x) when substituting.
steps.memory_tip: −(−cotx − x) = +cotx + x — two minus signs on a bracket flip both terms inside it.
